For claim c1:

United Church of Christ published an article on July 6, 2020, stating that the idea of 5G networks causing the spread of COVID-19 is a myth. The article cites the International Commission on Non-ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP), the World Health Organization (WHO), the Centers for Disease Control (CDC), and the U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) as sources that refute any link between 5G and the coronavirus. They explain that electromagnetic fields from 5G cannot carry viruses, and infection requires physical contact with the virus. [1]

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed on April 22, 2020, that there is no scientific basis for claims linking 5G technology to the spread of COVID-19. [2] [3] They stated that viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks, and COVID-19 has spread in countries without 5G. [4]

GOV.UK published information on May 6, 2020, also stating there is no evidence of a link between 5G and coronavirus. They highlight that scientific experts from the WHO and fact-checking organizations like Full Fact have rejected these theories. [4]

Boston University published an article on January 4, 2021, explaining that while 5G technology emits low levels of radiation, it is not significantly different from 4G and does not cause COVID-19. [5] They emphasize that COVID-19 is a viral disease caused by SARS-CoV-2. [5]

La Trobe University, in an article updated January 31, 2023, addresses the conspiracy theory that 5G spreads coronavirus, stating there is no evidence that 5G radio frequencies cause or exacerbate the spread of the coronavirus. [6] They clarify that radiation and viruses are different phenomena and do not interact. [6]

A study published in Medical Research Archives on April 12, 2021, found a statistically significant increase in COVID-19 cases and deaths in U.S. states and counties with 5G millimeter wave (mmW) technology compared to those without it. [7] The study notes that states with 5G mmW technology had higher cases and deaths per million. [7] However, it also states that the model only explains 28.74% of the variability in cases, indicating other factors are involved. [8]
